recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No core FHIR source work is needed for FHIR-11206 unless Patient Care later reopens AllergyIntolerance status handling; any future external terminology changes should proceed through the terminology/UTG process.
issue_request: FHIR-11206 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Patient Care change request for DSTU2 AllergyIntolerance asking to move entered-in-error out from under inactive in the AllergyIntolerance.status value set, place it at the same level as active and inactive, and align AllergyIntolerance with Condition.
initial_application: Git commit e7c9c0d32a1b91ac406c98fd0a2441fec2c625fb explicitly cited #11206 and removed Parent = #2 from the AllergyIntolerance entered-in-error status row. Later commit ed170ff0754268f2a677a011f9d432d1328415f0 applied related FHIR-11151 by replacing the old combined AllergyIntolerance.status with separate clinicalStatus and verificationStatus.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists AllergyIntolerance. The current StructureDefinition binds clinicalStatus to active/inactive/resolved and verificationStatus to unconfirmed/presumed/confirmed/refuted/entered-in-error. Local current terminology package artifacts show inactive has only resolved as a clinical child, while entered-in-error is a separate verification code; Condition uses the same verificationStatus pattern. FHIR-11207, the related narrative clarification, is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The original hierarchy defect is absent from current build-scope source and current terminology surfaces, and adding more prose would be redundant.

related_jiras.note: Published related issue split AllergyIntolerance.status into clinicalStatus and verificationStatus, explaining the current representation.
Published related issue fixed narrative wording that had treated entered-in-error as inactive; it is already represented on the combined branch.
